name: Collocational Error Detection
description: Detects collocational errors and unnatural word pairings — AI sometimes generates plausible but non-native collocations.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated text by identifying unnatural word combinations — collocations that are grammatically correct but not how native speakers actually express ideas. AI models sometimes produce subtly 'off' word pairings that reveal statistical generation rather than genuine language competence:

1. **Collocation Extraction and PMI Scoring**: The method extracts all bigram and trigram collocations from the text, focusing on five high-signal collocation types: (a) verb + noun ("make a decision" vs. *"do a decision"), (b) adjective + noun ("heavy rain" vs. *"strong rain"), (c) verb + preposition ("depend on" vs. *"depend of"), (d) adverb + adjective ("deeply concerned" vs. *"strongly concerned"), (e) noun + noun compounds ("blood pressure" vs. *"blood tension"). Each collocation is scored using pointwise mutual information (PMI) from the COCA corpus (560M words): PMI(w1,w2) = log₂[P(w1,w2) / (P(w1)×P(w2))]. Natural collocations score PMI > 3.0; unusual but acceptable collocations score 1.0–3.0; unnatural collocations score < 1.0 or appear in no corpus data. The method counts the proportion of collocations with PMI < 1.0: human text shows 2–5%; AI text shows 5–12%.

2. **Collocational Preference Violation Detection**: Many words have strong collocational preferences that native speakers internalize. The method maintains a database of the top-10 collocates for 5,000 common words (derived from the BNC and COCA corpora). For each content word in the text, the method checks whether its collocate is within the expected set. Three violation types are flagged: (a) near-synonym substitution — using a synonym that doesn't collocate ("do an effort" instead of "make an effort"), (b) semantic field confusion — choosing a collocate from the right semantic field but wrong conventional pairing ("perform a crime" instead of "commit a crime"), (c) register mismatch — formal collocate in informal context or vice versa ("conduct a chat" instead of "have a chat"). The violation rate per 1000 words: human text: 0.5–2.0; AI text: 2.0–6.0.

3. **Delexical Verb Collocation Analysis**: Delexical (light) verbs — "make", "do", "take", "have", "give", "get" — carry little meaning on their own but combine with nouns to form meaningful expressions. Their correct usage is highly conventionalized and language-specific: "make a mistake" (not *"do a mistake"), "take a shower" (not *"make a shower"), "have a look" (not *"take a look" — acceptable in some dialects but with different register). The method tallies all delexical verb constructions and checks each against a validated collocation database. Delexical verb error rate: human native text: < 1%; human non-native text: 3–8%; AI text: 1–4% (AI makes fewer but more subtle errors than non-native speakers, often producing unusual but not clearly wrong combinations).

4. **Collocational Fixedness and Substitutability**: The method checks whether fixed expressions are maintained intact: (a) completely fixed — idioms that cannot be modified ("kick the bucket" cannot become *"kick a bucket" or *"kick the pail"), (b) semi-fixed — expressions allowing limited substitution ("break the news/silence/ice" but not *"break the information"), (c) free combinations — fully substitutable word pairs. AI text sometimes shows: inappropriate modification of fixed expressions (inserting adjectives into idioms: *"kick the proverbial bucket"), substitution of near-synonyms in semi-fixed expressions, or over-creative variation of conventional collocations. The method measures fixedness violation rate: human text: < 0.5 per 1000 words; AI text: 0.5–2.0 per 1000 words.
parameters:
Collocation types: 5 (V+N, Adj+N, V+Prep, Adv+Adj, N+N)
PMI corpus: COCA (560M words)
Natural collocation PMI: > 3.0
Unnatural collocation PMI: < 1.0
Top-collocate database: 5000 words × 10 collocates
Human violation rate: 0.5–2.0 per 1000 words
AI violation rate: 2.0–6.0 per 1000 words
Delexical verbs: make, do, take, have, give, get
Minimum text length: 200 words
Minimum collocation count: 20
accuracy: 76–85% accuracy detecting AI-generated text via collocational error analysis. PMI scoring achieves AUC of 0.82. Delexical verb analysis adds 2–3% improvement. Performance best for non-technical prose; lower for specialized domains where unusual collocations may be domain-appropriate.
source: Sinclair, J. (1991). Corpus, Concordance, Collocation. Oxford University Press.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated text through subtle collocation unnaturalness. Identifying machine-translated text via transfer collocations. Evaluating natural language generation quality. Academic integrity checking for essays and reports.
strengths:
• Collocational knowledge is deeply conventionalized and hard to replicate
• PMI-based scoring provides objective, corpus-grounded measurement
• Delexical verb analysis targets a notoriously difficult area for non-native patterns
• Fixed expression checking catches idiom modification errors
• Complements grammar-checking with deeper lexical pattern analysis
limitations:
• Corpus coverage limits detection of domain-specific collocations
• Creative writing deliberately violates collocational norms
• Regional English varieties have different collocational preferences
• Non-native human writers also produce collocational errors
• Advanced AI models are improving at natural collocations
